liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Rider** (1 review): Played at a fast pace, so Rider is barely recognizable [11]
- **Next Time You See Me** (1 review): Garcia's guitar tone and playing are singled out as perfect [13]
- **Stealin'** (1 review): Pigpen's organ playing really shows during this song [13]
- **Cardboard Cowboy** (1 review): Reviewer believes this is the only live performance of the song ever [6]
- **Viola Lee Blues** (1 review): Segues are longer and the jam is harder and more experimental, very hot for 1966 [5]
- **It's All Over Now Baby Blue** (1 review): Reviewer finds Baby Blue fantastic here, and it stayed with them [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Standing On The Corner**: rare: 6 archived performances [16]
- **Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 13 archived performances [16]
- **You Don't. Have To Ask**: rare: 7 archived performances [16]
- **Stealin'**: rare: 14 archived performances [16]
- **Cardboard Cowboy**: rare: 4 archived performances [16]
- **Cream Puff War**: rare: 12 archived performances [16]
- **Like a Dog (lyrics by Robert Hunter, music by David Gans) 11/11/00, Fillmore**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **Bird Song 11/7/00 Solana Beach, CA**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Baby Blue [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-07-29.sbd.2243.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 62 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd66-07-29.sbd.vernon.9051.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 55 min; rated 4.39/5 by 23 [2]. Said about its sound: Rated about 3.75 to 4; a bit fuzzy but fully audible, good for a 1960s recording; Guitars and organ throughout recall a 60s a-go-go, surf music sound; Pigpen's organ is cranked loud in the mix, and the quality is strong for 1966 [7][8][15]
- **gd1966-07-29.sbd.GEMS.94633.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 55 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [3]

## Around the show

- The show opens with a greeting from Captain Consciousness [8]
- The date is uncertain; two different setlists are offered for it, and an info file explains the confusion [2]
- Reviewer calls this a turning point for Viola Lee Blues compared with all earlier 1966 shows on the archive [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-07-29.sbd.2243.sbeok.shnf**: source: probably MR>C>DAT>CDR>EAC>WAV>SHN [1]. Also: David Gans broadcast this on his Dead to the World show on KPFA, 11/30/00, from a pre-FM CDR [1]
- **gd66-07-29.sbd.vernon.9051.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Soundboard source passed through MR to CDR, via Raoul Duke, then seeded to etree by Matt Vernon [2]
- **gd1966-07-29.sbd.GEMS.94633.flac16**: source: SBD > 10" 1/2 track 15ips MR [3]. Also: This copy upgrades earlier circulating versions of the show [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead P.N.E. Garden Auditorium - July 29, 1966](https://www.dead.net/show/july-29-1966) [17]
- Fan art by musictap.com: [2CD 50th Anniversary Deluxe Edition Of The Grateful Dead Arrives In January](https://musictap.com/2016/11/16/2cd-50th-anniversary-deluxe-edition-of-the-grateful-dead-arrives-in-january/) [18]
